intent.note: Clause (3) 'redispatch calls dispatch without the member's tree ... take the tree from state.wave.trees as the resume branch already does': apply_answer's redispatch now passes ((state.get('wave') or {}).get('trees') or {}).get(task['id']) to dispatch(..., 'reviewer', tree), the same expression the resume branch uses; open_dispatch then records tree_head of that tree. Clause (4) 'with executor.writerModel unset, resume on red-refused-writer / clauses-uncovered-writer stops with answer retry, which those decisions do not offer ... offer retry ... or name what works': both are done. red_refused and clauses_uncovered raise the -writer decision only while writer_path_on(ctx), so the plain red-refused / clauses-uncovered (DECISIONS offers retry|block) is asked instead. A -writer decision already pending when the setting went away now stops with without_writer_way(), derived from DECISIONS (retry where offered, else block --reason or restore the setting). Clause (5) 'cap_note says still red though clause and red-first rounds spend the same budget - say what spent them': open_dispatch records a kind (RESUME_KINDS) on resume dispatches and cap_note labels each round by it and states that all kinds spend one budget. A round with no kind is named by number only. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately: the three code changes, the RESUME_KINDS table and the new test blocks sr2, wo, ck all appear in the diff. Its stamp compares `current`. Its dependants answer holds: open_dispatch only gained an optional keyword and no decision name changed. The one dependant it leaves stale is the guide sentence in finding 1. Not changed: gate_red_decision still raises gate-red-writer without checking writer_path_on. That is correct because gate-red-writer offers retry and the stop names it.
